economy.summary: He lists industrialisation, ease of doing business and SME support as aims, without measures or costings.
economy.analysis: Leadership's May 2026 report lists industrialisation, easier business conditions and targeted support for small and medium enterprises among his pledges. In 2023 he pledged to reduce oil dependence within one year. No positions on the exchange rate, subsidy, inflation, tax or trade were found.
missing: Positions on exchange rate, subsidy, inflation and tax

security.summary: He promises to equip and direct security agencies against insurgents, prosecute their enablers, adopt modern technology and send an executive bill for state and community policing.
security.analysis:
Security is one of the three priorities Nwanyanwu named in his May 2026 acceptance speech, alongside unity and corruption. According to NAN and Premium Times, he would immediately equip and direct security agencies to 'smoke out' insurgents nationwide, prosecute arrested suspects quickly, and also prosecute collaborators, enablers and facilitators. He would acquire and develop modern technology for security, and he would send an executive bill to the National Assembly to establish state and community policing. Leadership adds more funding for security agencies and better welfare for personnel.

The state-policing bill is the most concrete institutional proposal. Because policing is federal under the 1999 Constitution, such a change would need a constitutional amendment passed by the National Assembly and approved by state assemblies. Proposing an executive bill acknowledges that route but cannot guarantee its outcome. The rhetoric of eliminating insurgents 'without mercy' is not paired with any statement on human-rights safeguards. No costs, timelines or reforms of command structures were stated. He has no record of overseeing security institutions; at the 2014 National Conference he was a Labour Party delegate, but no record of his security positions there was reviewed.
strengths: Names a legal instrument (executive bill) for its central reform
unknowns: Design of the proposed state and community police

leadership.summary: He has led national organisations for decades (a bank workers' union, the Labour Party for about ten years and the ZLP), but has not led a government institution.
leadership.analysis:
Nwanyanwu's leadership record is in trade unions and political parties. Daily Trust's 2023 profile says he rose through the National Union of Banks, Insurance and Financial Institutions Employees to become its national president in 1989, which made him a member of the Nigeria Labour Congress's National Executive Council. He then chaired the Labour Party, which emerged from the NLC-backed Party for Social Democracy, for about ten years. During that period the party won the Ondo governorship with Olusegun Mimiko, a point reported by Wikipedia and not independently confirmed here. He handed over in 2014 and became chairman of the Board of Trustees. In February 2015 he resigned that post and left the party, saying his advice to reposition it was rejected and objecting to how candidates for the 2015 elections were nominated.

He later became National Chairman of the Zenith Labour Party, which he still led in December 2025 and May 2026. He was its presidential candidate in 2023 and again in 2027. He thus combines the roles of party chairman and candidate, as some other small-party candidates do. He also served as Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of Adekunle Ajasin University; the dates and his record there were not found.
strengths: Long record of leading national membership organisations
limitations: Record as university council chair undocumented
unknowns: Dates and outcomes of his pro-chancellorship

integrity.summary: No court case, investigation or allegation against him was found; this reflects limited coverage, not a confirmed clean record. He campaigns on investigating unexplained wealth.
integrity.analysis: No integrity matters were found in the sources reviewed. His 2015 exit from the Labour Party cited concerns about the integrity of candidate nomination. No asset declaration was found.

experience.summary: No elected public office. Decades in banking, trade unionism and party leadership; a lawyer; Labour Party chairman for about ten years; ZLP presidential candidate in 2023 with 77,665 votes.
experience.analysis:
Nwanyanwu has not held elected or ministerial office, so his experience is in organised labour, law and party politics. INEC lists his age as 66 and his qualifications as FSLC, WAEC, LLB and LLM. Daily Trust reports that he was born in 1959 in Amuzu-Amaimo, Ikeduru LGA, Imo State. He attended St James Primary School, Amuzu, and Oraifite Boys' High School in Anambra State, and studied labour-management relations at Howard University's School of Business. He worked at Union Bank from 1979 to 1993. Wikipedia, used here only as a pointer, adds NIPSS membership (1992), a law degree (1998), call to the Bar (2000) and an LLM from the University of Lagos; these are consistent with the LLB and LLM on INEC's list.

He chaired the Labour Party for about a decade, left it in February 2015, and later chaired the ZLP. He was the ZLP's 2023 presidential candidate. INEC's declared results, as reported by Nairametrics, gave him 77,665 of 24,025,940 valid votes, about 0.3 per cent. He was made an Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic in 2012 and served as Pro-Chancellor of Adekunle Ajasin University. His running mate for 2027 is Hassan Khalid, aged 37.
strengths: Long institutional experience in unions and party leadership
Has contested a presidential election before
unknowns: Dates of his law practice and university council service

vision.summary: He frames his candidacy around national unity as an 'emergency', citizens' rights, security and anti-corruption, continuing themes from his 2023 run.
vision.analysis:
Nwanyanwu's 2027 vision puts national unity first. In his May 2026 acceptance speech he said his government would treat unity as a national emergency because ethnic and religious divisions and mismanaged diversity have weakened the country. He promised inclusive government, restored citizens' rights and regional 'building blocks', and said he aims to make Nigeria a hub for economic and social prosperity. The themes continue from his 2023 campaign. Daily Trust then reported pledges to guarantee fundamental rights, avoid rule by decree, build trust across ethnic lines, give traditional and religious leaders roles in nation-building, and reduce oil dependence within one year.

The vision is consistent across both campaigns, which allows comparison over time. It is mostly framed in principles rather than policies, however. 'Building blocks' and the role of traditional rulers are not defined. The 2023 one-year target for reducing oil dependence was not repeated in the 2026 reports reviewed, and no costed programme accompanies the unity agenda. His public commentary as party chairman, such as advising former President Jonathan not to run in 2027, shows engagement with national politics but adds no policy content.

foreign.analysis: Leadership mentions attracting investment as an economic aim, but no positions on ECOWAS, trade or security cooperation were found.

humanImpact.summary: No social-protection proposals were found beyond restoring citizens' rights and youth confidence.
humanImpact.analysis: His pledges concern rights, unity and youth confidence; no welfare, poverty-reduction or social-protection programmes were found.

promises.summary: His 2027 promises are a state and community policing bill, prosecution of insurgents' enablers, investigation of unexplained wealth, and general economic and power-sector aims; none is costed or time-bound.
promises.analysis:
The commitments reported from Nwanyanwu's May 2026 acceptance speech and the party's endorsement are mostly declaratory. The most specific is a promise to send an executive bill to the National Assembly to create state and community policing. Others include equipping security agencies, prosecuting insurgents together with their collaborators, enablers and facilitators, investigating and sanctioning individuals and groups with unexplained wealth, and treating national unity as an emergency. On the economy and power, Leadership reports aims of industrialisation, ease of doing business, SME support, private participation and renewable investment.

None of these promises carries a target, timeline or cost. Several depend on bodies outside the presidency. State policing needs a constitutional amendment that also requires state assemblies' approval. Prosecutions depend on the courts and on prosecutorial independence. An unexplained-wealth regime would need legal backing, which may require new legislation. Because he ran in 2023 on similar themes, a reviewer could compare the two platforms, but no 2023 manifesto was retrieved. The commitments are listed under plans.
strengths: The central institutional reform is tied to a stated legislative route
limitations: Heavy dependence on legislature, states and courts
unknowns: Draft of the proposed policing bill
